newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-JAMAICA FRIENDLY IN MEXICO ENDS IN BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JAMAICA FRIENDLY IN MEXICO ENDS IN BRAWL.

text.p: A friendly soccer match between Jamaica's national team and a Mexican first division squad ended in a pitched battle on Tuesday that forced the referee to scrap the game.
Several Mexican players were injured when members of Toros Neza and the Jamaican squad punched and kicked each other for five minutes during the match.
Several Jamaican players then stormed off the field and returned waving bricks and broken glass to hold the angry Mexican side at bay.

Jamaica was leading Toros Neza 1-0 in the 19th minute when a Jamaican mid-fielder slid hard into Toros' Argentine-born German Arangio. He got to his feet and punched the Jamaican tackler and an all-out fight ensued.
The Jamaican squad was in Mexico to prepare for its April 13 World Cup qualifying match against hosts Mexico, which currently lead the CONCACAF region standings.
The Mexican first division squad said the Jamaicans were playing far too dirty on Tuesday, tackling hard and trying to provoke them.
"That is not normal behaviour. It isn't possible that they react like this in a friendly," said Neza's Argentine striker Antonio Mohamed.
Brazilian-born Jamaica coach Rene Simoes defended his players, saying they lacked international experience.
